questions.stem: At Fernway, the lakehouse table holds over 100,000 small files. Which command rewrites them into fewer, larger files?
questions.explanation: OPTIMIZE compacts small files into larger ones, which speeds up reads. VACUUM removes files no longer referenced by the table.

options.text: A way to sort pipeline activities
A write-time optimization of Parquet files that makes reads faster across Fabric engines

questions.explanation: V-Order reorganizes the Parquet layout when files are written (row-group distribution, encoding and compression), so Fabric engines read them faster. The files stay standard Parquet.

questions.stem: What does VACUUM do to a Delta table?

options.text: It deletes data files no longer referenced by the table and older than the retention period, which limits time travel to that period
It deletes the table's history and data

questions.explanation: VACUUM frees storage by removing old, unreferenced files. Time travel to versions that needed those files stops working. The default retention is seven days.

questions.stem: Most queries on a large lakehouse table filter on DeviceId. Which option can improve data skipping for those queries when you optimize the table?
questions.explanation: Z-ordering co-locates related values in the same files, so filters on DeviceId can skip more files.

questions.stem: You run `OPTIMIZE dbo.sales ZORDER BY (region, customer_id) VORDER`. Put the operations Spark applies in order.
questions.explanation: When Z-Order and V-order are combined in one command, Spark applies bin compaction, then Z-Order, then V-order.

questions.stem: You run the lakehouse's table maintenance from the portal with VACUUM and a retention of 2 days, and the request fails. What is the reason?

options.text: Portal and API maintenance requests fail by default for retention intervals under seven days
The table must be a Hive table in Parquet format
VACUUM can only run on tables that use V-Order
VACUUM can only run from a pipeline's Lakehouse Maintenance activity

questions.explanation: The default retention threshold is seven days and shorter intervals fail unless `spark.databricks.delta.retentionDurationCheck.enabled` is set to false. A shorter retention also reduces time travel history.

questions.stem: An engineer can't run table maintenance on a lakehouse table that was created as a legacy Hive table in CSV format. Why?

options.text: Table maintenance needs the table to be partitioned
Table maintenance runs only on tables smaller than 1 GB
Table maintenance needs V-Order to be enabled in the workspace
Table maintenance applies only to Delta tables

questions.explanation: Table maintenance applies only to Delta tables; legacy Hive tables in formats such as Parquet, ORC, AVRO or CSV aren't supported.

questions.stem: A streaming ingestion job appends small batches to a Delta table every minute, and the table keeps collecting small files. You want files compacted automatically after writes, without scheduling OPTIMIZE. What should you enable?
questions.explanation: Auto compaction checks partition health after each write and runs a synchronous OPTIMIZE when there are too many small files. OPTIMIZE FULL is costly and meant to run rarely, and VACUUM only removes unreferenced files.

questions.stem: A scheduled OPTIMIZE job keeps rewriting bins of files even when merging them barely improves the layout. Which setting skips compaction of bins that aren't likely to improve performance?
questions.explanation: Fast optimize analyzes files and skips compaction that isn't likely to help, which lowers write amplification. The other settings control V-Order, VACUUM checks and shuffle.

questions.stem: You want the files that OPTIMIZE rewrites in table `dbo.sales` to have V-Order applied. Which two approaches achieve this? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Set `delta.parquet.vorder.enabled` = true on the table, then run `OPTIMIZE dbo.sales`
Run `OPTIMIZE dbo.sales ZORDER BY (region)` with V-Order off in the session and table

questions.explanation: OPTIMIZE with VORDER forces V-Order, and OPTIMIZE without it inherits the table property when set. VACUUM doesn't rewrite files, the old setting is removed in runtime 1.3, and Z-Order alone doesn't apply V-Order.
